locator.text: Equation (4.28), p. 33, in the statement of Theorem 4.6

evidence: paper: M(\infty,\eta) = J(\infty,\eta) = S(\infty,\eta) = 0,\qquad \int_0^\infty (H - H_{\mathrm{pow}})\,dX = 0,\qquad H_{\mathrm{pow}} = \sqrt{2X}\,c_\infty X^{-A},

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The rewriting is from the paper's cumulative radial integrals at X = ∞ to Lebesgue integrals over Ioi 0. The paper's M, I, J, S of (4.15) are ∫_0^X of the densities U, H, U·H, U²−E²/2; its M(∞,η)=J(∞,η)=S(∞,η)=0 therefore says ∫_0^∞ U = 0, ∫_0^∞ U·H = 0, ∫_0^∞ (U²−E²/2) = 0. FiveMomentCertificate's mass_zero, transport_zero, energy_zero are literally those three with H expanded as √(2X)·E (the paper's (4.8) H = √(2X)E; Lean's Witness.H p = Real.sqrt (2 * p.1) * W.E p, NominalProfile.lean:2498), and angular_zero is ∫_0^∞ (√(2X)E − powerH X) = 0, i.e. the paper's ∫_0^∞ (H − H_pow) dX = 0. The limit-of-cumulative-integrals form and the Lebesgue-integral form agree because the same structure carries the four IntegrableOn … (Ioi 0) hypotheses, so the cumulative integrals converge and the limit is the integral. H_pow matches term by term: OutgoingDilation.powerH F XR X = √(2X) · powerE F XR X and powerE_coefficient rewrites powerE F XR X as (powerConstant F.data · XR^(1/2+h)) · X^(−(1/2+h)), so c_∞ = powerConstant F.data · XR^A, which does not mention η — the paper's "c_∞ > 0 is independent of η" — and powerConstant_pos gives its positivity. This is the same c_∞ that appears in the prefactor of (4.29): see the two-line computation recorded under eq-4.29, carrierAmplitude F · (switchRadius F XR)^A = powerConstant F.data · XR^A. Witness.five_moments asserts the certificate for every eta in HeatedOutgoing.parameterDomain, matching the paper's quantification over η.
